title: Godly Ministry and the Flock of Christ
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: Godly Ministry Does Not Purposefully Hurt the Flock
subpoints: Paul uses sarcasm to expose the foolishness of accepting abusive leaders
False apostles enslaved, devoured, and physically abused the Corinthians
Paul contrasts his meekness with the arrogance of the 'super-apostles'
Leaders must serve as servants, not masters, seeking the good of the flock

outline.title: Godly Ministry Willingly Suffers for the Sake of the Gospel
subpoints: Paul boasts in his infirmities and sufferings as evidence of his ministry
Physical hardships include stripes, prisons, shipwrecks, and perils
Suffering is a mark of authentic apostolic authority
The goal is the salvation and sanctification of the elect

summary:
In this sermon, Pastor Tito Lyro concludes the expository series on 2 Corinthians by examining Paul’s response to the 'super-apostles' who had infiltrated the Corinthian church. The message focuses on two primary characteristics of godly ministry: it does not purposefully hurt the flock, and it willingly suffers for the sake of the gospel. Paul’s use of sarcasm in 2 Corinthians 11 is highlighted not as a model for general communication, but as a strategic tool to dismantle the false credentials of abusive leaders who exploited the congregation financially and physically.

The sermon contrasts the behavior of the false apostles, who enslaved and devoured the believers, with Paul’s own ministry of meekness and self-denial. Paul’s willingness to endure hardships—such as beatings, imprisonment, and shipwrecks—is presented as the true evidence of his apostolic authority, rather than the worldly boasting of his opponents. This suffering is not for self-glorification but for the benefit of the churches.

The application extends beyond pastoral leadership to all believers who hold positions of influence, such as parents, teachers, and mentors. The call is to lead as servants rather than masters, viewing those under one’s care as people to be loved and invested in, rather than resources to be exploited. The ultimate goal of such ministry is the glory of God and the spiritual growth of His people.
